sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell a house in Fort Myers?
sections.html:
In Fort Myers you can hire an agent, handle the sale yourself, or accept money from a buyer who takes the house exactly as it stands. Each route trades price against time, repair work and certainty.

A listing usually reaches the widest pool of buyers, but it comes with showings, inspections and a buyer's lender. A cash sale skips most of that. The price is often lower, and you decide whether the speed is worth it for your situation.

  • Listing: more exposure, more steps, a closing date that depends on the buyer's financing.
  • Selling yourself: no listing agent, but you handle pricing, paperwork and negotiation.
  • Cash offer: fewer contingencies, as-is condition, a closing date you can often choose.

sections.h2: What is the Fort Myers housing market like on paper?
sections.html:
Census data describes a city of 101,581 people in mid 2025, up 17.5 percent from the April 2020 estimates base of 86,424. That pace of growth shapes who is buying and who is renting.

The same Census page lists a typical owner-occupied value of $384,500 across 2020 to 2024 and a median gross rent of $1,580. About 49.1 percent of units are owner-occupied, so roughly half the city's households rent. Persons over 65 make up 23.2 percent of residents, workers average a 25.2 minute commute, and median household income is $63,732 in 2024 dollars. Those figures point to a mix of long-time owners, retirees and working households, so buyers and renters for your house come from several groups.

sections.h2: How did Fort Myers develop, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Fort Myers began as an army post on the Caloosahatchee River, and the city was incorporated on August 12, 1885. Its older neighborhoods near the river carry that early street grid.

The Edison and Ford Winter Estates history of the city notes that Thomas Edison bought his riverfront property in 1885 and that Fort Myers broke from Monroe County in 1887 to create Lee County. McGregor Boulevard took its present name on July 15, 1914. Houses along those older corridors can be decades old, which affects what an inspector looks at: roofs, wiring, plumbing and windows.

The Fort Myers Community Redevelopment Agency says it has managed redevelopment trusts since 1984 to address blighted areas. Its listed programs include residential grants, commercial grants, historic preservation and affordable housing development. If your house sits in a redevelopment area, ask the agency whether a grant program applies before you sell or renovate.

sections.h2: Which Fort Myers offices handle permits and records?
sections.html:
The city runs an online permitting and licensing portal for building permits, and Lee County offices handle assessment, taxes and recorded documents. Start with the right office for the question.

  • Open or expired building permits: check the city's online permit portal, because a buyer's title and inspection process often asks about them.
  • Value, homestead and exemptions: the Lee County Property Appraiser, whose site offers a parcel search and explains homestead and portability.
  • Deeds and recorded liens: the Lee County Clerk's Official Records search, which the appraiser's site points to.
  • Tax bills: the Lee County tax collector. Ask what is owed through the closing date.

Unpermitted work is a common snag on older Fort Myers houses. Resolve it, or tell the buyer plainly, before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees come with a Fort Myers sale?
sections.html:
The deed carries Florida documentary stamp tax of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration under s. 201.02(1)(a), and state revenue officials say all parties to the document are liable for it, whoever agrees to pay.

The clerk charges recording fees on top of that. Under s. 28.24(13) the first page is $5.00 and each added page is $4.00, with separate trust fund and technology charges. Your title company will total these on the settlement statement.

Property tax runs on its own calendar. Assessment is set each January 1, the TRIM notice arrives in August, and bills go out in November with a discount of 4 percent for paying that month. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1. Ask the Lee County tax collector for the amount due as of your closing date.

sections.h2: What happens to the homestead exemption and the assessment cap when I sell?
sections.html:
A sale ends your homestead on that property, and the new owner's assessment resets to just value the next January 1.

The Save Our Homes cap limits yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The Department of Revenue's chart shows a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent. That protection stays with the old house, but you may transfer part of that benefit to a new Florida homestead if you establish it within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, filing DR-501T with DR-501 by March 1.

  • Homestead exemption: up to $50,000, filed on DR-501 by March 1.
  • Renting the home ends the exemption.
  • Portability is a benefit to plan before you close, not after.

sections.h2: What if the Fort Myers house is inherited or in foreclosure?
sections.html:
Both situations have fixed timelines in Florida law, and both can still end in a sale.

For an inherited house, summary administration is allowed when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or the person died more than two years ago (s. 735.201). A deed from a personal representative under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not taxable for doc stamps. Creditors must file within the later of 3 months after first publication or 30 days after service (s. 733.702).

In a foreclosure, the final judgment sets a public sale 20 to 35 days out, the high bidder posts a 5 percent deposit, and objections are due within 10 days of the certificate of sale (s. 45.031). Selling before that date can end the case and protect what equity you have. Ask the Lee County Clerk about any surplus funds after a sale.

sections.h2: How do tenants affect selling a Fort Myers house?
sections.html:
Renters can stay through a sale unless the lease or notice rules end the tenancy first, and a rental share of about half the city's occupied housing means this comes up often.

Under s. 83.57, a month-to-month tenancy ends with at least 30 days' notice before the end of a monthly period. Year-to-year needs 60 days, and week-to-week needs 7. A fixed lease generally travels with the property.

Tell any cash buyer about the lease at the start. Some buyers want the house vacant, and others will buy it with the tenant in place. Keep rent records and the signed lease ready.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Fort Myers house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, a cash buyer can take the house with its flaws. Expect the price to reflect the repairs the buyer will take on, and ask for the offer in writing before you compare it with a listing.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Fort Myers deed?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue says all parties to the document are liable, whichever side agrees to pay. In practice the contract assigns it, and the closing agent collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Does the Fort Myers owner-occupied rate affect my sale?
faqs.a: Only indirectly. With about 49.1 percent of units owner-occupied, many buyers are investors or landlords, and they tend to ask about rent rolls and lease terms.

faqs.q: What deadline should I know for homestead after a sale?
faqs.a: File DR-501 and any DR-501T with the Lee County Property Appraiser by March 1 for the tax year. Portability needs the new homestead to be set within three years of January 1 of the year you left the old one.

faqs.q: Where do I confirm my current tax balance?
faqs.a: Ask the Lee County tax collector for the amount due through your closing date. Florida bills in November, and unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1.
